evidence.fitness: Job walked: a billing partner pastes one quarter's timekeeper productivity report (recorded value, billed, collected) to find where realization leaks and who to talk to first. With annual figures and clean cut-offs it does the job well, and the dollar ranking plus pre/post split is exactly the conversation starter a managing partner wants. But collected > billed for any timekeeper is a hard error (calc.mjs:79), and on a period-basis report (receipts in the period vs bills issued in the period) that is common for a quarter, and not rare for a year, when prior-period receivables are paid. The user cannot proceed without editing their own figures. No import of a billing-system export, so a 30-timekeeper firm types 150 numbers.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard law-firm billing definitions (dollar basis, as in large-firm financial reporting): realization = billed / (hours x standard rate), collection = collected / billed, yield or collected realization = collected / standard value; Clio Legal Trends Report uses the same three-stage chain (utilization -> realization -> collection) on hours; lockup as WIP days + debtor days (the standard lockup measure used in law-firm finance). Matches: all three ratios, their product identity, lockup on standard value per day and billing per day, utilization as recorded hours / available hours, effective rate as cash per recorded hour, billed above standard (premium/fixed fee) allowed as realization > 100%. Departs: treating collection > 100% as a data error rather than the normal period-basis effect of collecting prior billings; no option for an 'on matched cohort' vs 'period' basis, which practitioners distinguish.

defects.what: Collected above billed is a hard validation error, but on period-basis reports (receipts in the period vs bills issued in the period) collections routinely exceed billings for a timekeeper in a quarter, and sometimes a year, when prior-period receivables are paid. The user cannot get any result without editing their real figures. It should be computed (collection > 100%) with a warning, not refused.

The findings a partner acts on are untested: inverting which stage loses more (pre- vs post-bill) or changing the top-leak share denominator leaves all 28 tests green; the sample test only checks the yield string.
README says usage counters are 'opt-in-only ... off by default'; usage.mjs counts unless the visitor opts out or sends DNT/GPC (the page correctly says opt-out-able). Counts never leave the device.

When billing exceeds standard (pre-bill gain) and part goes unpaid, the finding calls the post-bill loss 'the larger half of the loss' though it exceeds the total loss (e.g. $9,000 of a $5,000 net loss).
Point value is computed from the collection rate already rounded to 4 decimals, so the headline 'value of a point' is off by about $1 on the sample ($21,445.73 vs $21,446.74).
Accounting negatives such as '(1,000)' parse to null and the user is told the figure is missing rather than that it cannot be negative.
Error status says 'Fix the highlighted figures' but no input is highlighted; only the first invalid one is focused.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: every headline figure on the shipped example (realization 85.05%, collection 89.32%, yield 75.97%, the dollar ranking, 29.8% top share, lockup 31.92 + 67.92 days, the target as 8,563.6 hours or an 83.3% yield) matches an independent recomputation from the standard dollar-basis definitions, and the page states its formulas and limits honestly. It misses the bar on verification: 3 of 5 seeded mutants survived, including inverting the pre- vs post-bill finding a partner reads first. It is held back as a working tool by treating collections above billings as an error, which a billing partner entering a quarter's period reports will hit and cannot get past. Small fixes: compute collection > 100% with a warning, pin the findings in tests, correct the README's opt-in wording, use the unrounded collection rate for point value.
